db_evidence.notes: The `entities` table names 'Wang Lingguan' (王灵官) only once, at 77190-77460s (a boss-defeat/victory-screen event: '已击败 王灵官'). All 5 rollouts' semantic_search and run_sql calls converged on this single tagged occurrence and never explored earlier timeline regions, so they never saw the question's actual clue windows at 49096-49146 and 61850-61877 (roughly 12,000-28,000s earlier). Directly inspecting those two windows: event_steps at 49110-49140 describes 'staff-carrying figure touches the illuminated panel on the pagoda, releasing purple particle effects', and event_steps at 61830-61860 describes 'player approaches stone arch/pillar with plaque and touches it, triggering glowing purple effect' immediately followed (61860-61920) by a fight against a golden-armored, white-winged boss -- a plausible unnamed first encounter with Wang Lingguan that the entity extractor never tagged with that name. Frames pulled at 49110s and 61850s (via `memcli.py frame`) visually confirm both are the same recurring pagoda/monument 'touch to reveal' interaction, structurally identical across the two clue windows. A targeted SQL keyword scan for pagoda/plaque/arch + purple/touch/reveal before 62000s found only these 2 occurrences in event_steps text (not 4), so the DB text alone does not obviously yield the reference count of 4 either -- getting to '4 talismans' likely requires recognizing this game-specific 'shrine reveal' mechanic and finding 2 more such occurrences elsewhere in the timeline, or a different definition of 'reveal' than any rollout attempted. No rollout attempted this at all; all 5 stayed inside the 75000-77250s window.

root_causes: Single point of anchoring failure: the memory DB's `entities` table names 'Wang Lingguan' only at the 77190s boss-defeat/victory screen, so every semantic_search for 'Wang Lingguan' (across episodes, event_steps, entities tables, with many paraphrases) converged on that one occurrence and none of the 5 independent rollouts ever looked earlier in the timeline where the question's actual clue windows (49096-49146, 61850-61877) sit.

The clue windows correspond to a recurring 'touch pagoda/shrine, release purple particles' interaction that is not textually tagged with the word 'talisman' in the DB captions, so even a keyword search for 'talisman' before 62000s (which does return dozens of unrelated talisman-menu-browsing rows throughout the video) would not have flagged these two rows as the relevant evidence without visual inspection.

Within the wrong (77000-77200s) window, the equipment/menu icons there are ambiguous general-purpose UI icons (masks, charms, consumables, quick-items), not a clean 'talisman reveal' sequence; clip_qa readings of essentially the same seconds disagreed sharply (3, 3, 3, 0, 13), showing the visual sub-agent's counting is unreliable on this ambiguous content -- a symptom, not the root cause, of being in the wrong place.

No rollout used the disagreement between its own visual read and the general-retrieval expectation (e.g. rollout 3 finding 0 talismans in the anchor window) as a signal to search elsewhere; they treated a clean negative/positive local read as sufficient rather than reconsidering the anchor entity.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly followed the general retrieval workflow (read_skill -> semantic_search -> run_sql narrowing -> clip_qa verification -> submit) and used clip_qa to visually verify counts rather than guessing from text alone.
Rollout 3's clip_qa correctly identified that the 77070-77190s window shows masks/armor, not talismans, which is a locally accurate visual read even though it was applied to the wrong window.
transferable_lessons: When a named entity/boss has only a single DB-tagged occurrence, do not assume that occurrence is the one the question refers to (especially for 'before facing X' questions with a Long temporal_certificate) -- explicitly search earlier in the timeline for unnamed encounters matching the boss's visual description (e.g. iconography, mythological role) before committing to the tagged occurrence.

For 'reveal N of <item>' counting questions, treat sharp disagreement across repeated clip_qa calls on the same seconds (3 vs 3 vs 3 vs 0 vs 13) as a strong signal that the window itself is wrong or the target action is being misidentified, and use it to trigger a broader relocation search rather than trusting a single visual count.

Search for the target action/mechanic itself (e.g. 'touching a monument that releases particles', 'reveal') across the whole timeline via multiple SQL keyword variants and semantic_search, not just for the named entity, since recurring gameplay mechanics may repeat with the same visual signature at multiple untagged locations.
